title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The ambient object is a finite 1-dimensional combinatorial 'multiplicity' M, as in the neighbouring pages. M = M_0 ∪ M_1 with M_0 = L. L is the set of points or vertices. M_1 is the set of open 'intervals' S_ab = S_{a,b}, whose endpoints satisfy a ◁ S_ab and b ◁ S_ab. In effect it is a cell decomposition of a 1-manifold, essentially a subdivided line. A 'préfigure' Φ is an arbitrary subset of M, i.e. a constructible subset of the line given cell by cell. Its closure Φ̄ adds to Φ all endpoints of its intervals. Write Φ_0 = Φ ∩ L for its points and Φ_1 = Φ ∩ M_1 for its intervals.

This page is a 'parenthèse' (zoology) classifying the vertices of Φ. It serves the programme of the previous page: an 'autodual' description of constructible supports by normalised (irredundant) préfigures.

Definitions.
- The vertex set is δΦ = Φ̄ ∩ L = (Φ̄)_0. Proper vertices are those in Φ_0; improper vertices are those in δΦ \ Φ_0.
- The order of a vertex is ord(a,Φ) = card{X ∈ Φ_1 | a ◁ X}. It lies in {0,1,2} because each vertex of a subdivided 1-manifold bounds at most two intervals.

Lemma. If a ∈ δΦ and ord(a,Φ) = 0, then a ∈ Φ. Proof: a point of Φ̄ \ Φ must be an endpoint of some interval of Φ. Hence the isolated vertices satisfy Φ_is = {s ∈ δΦ | ord = 0} ⊂ Φ_0.

Further classes.
- Order 1: boundary vertices ∂Φ. These split into proper ones, ∂_0Φ = Φ_0 ∩ ∂Φ ⊂ Φ, and improper ones.
- Order 2: internal vertices δ_int Φ. The next page splits these into proper ones (redundant, 'de morcellement': the point could be erased by merging the two adjacent intervals) and improper ones (lacunary: a puncture).

This gives five combinatorial types: isolated, proper boundary, improper boundary, redundant interior, lacunary interior.

Example. Take the subdivided segment a–b–c–d plus a point e, with Φ = {a, S_ab, S_bc, c, S_cd, e}.
- Φ̄ = {a, S_ab, b, S_bc, c, S_cd, d, e}.
- ∂Φ = {a, d}.
- e is isolated, a is proper boundary, d is improper boundary, c is redundant, b is lacunary.

Purpose. Normalised préfigures are those with no redundant vertices. The duality sought on p.107 exchanges proper and improper vertices, i.e. Φ versus its complement in its closure. The classification prepares that.
errors: The transcription line 'sommets propres : ceux de 𝔏_0 = 𝔏̄ ∩ L' should read Φ_0 = Φ ∩ L (Φ̄ ∩ L is δΦ itself). The image seems to have Φ_0 ⊂ δΦ with Φ ∩ L intended.
Minor variable slip: in the definition of Φ_is, Grothendieck writes ord(a,Φ) while the bound variable is s.

The claim ord ∈ {0,1,2} silently assumes the ambient multiplicity is 1-manifold-like (each vertex bounds at most two intervals). It fails for general graphs, but is fine in the line/curve context of these notes.

The first block on the page is crossed out and rewritten below; it contains the same definitions plus a half-finished guess 'δΦ =? {a ∈ L | ord(a,Φ) = ...}'. That guess is rightly abandoned, since ord-0 vertices of δΦ must be checked separately via the Lemma.

ideas.what: Combinatorial description of constructible subsets of a subdivided line as sets of open cells and points, with closure, vertex set and boundary.
ideas.modern_name: cell decomposition of definable/semi-algebraic subsets of R (o-minimal 1-dimensional cell decomposition); subcomplexes/partial complexes of a CW or simplicial complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (semi-algebraic geometry, Łojasiewicz; o-minimality van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6; no detailed combinatorics published

ideas.what: Five-fold classification of vertices of a 1-dimensional constructible set by order (0,1,2) and properness: isolated, proper/improper boundary, redundant ('morcellement')/lacunary interior.
ideas.modern_name: local types of points of a 1-dimensional constructible set; local Euler characteristic / link types

ideas.what: Lemma: a vertex of the closure of order 0 lies in Φ (isolated points are genuine points).

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary bookkeeping classification of cell-vertices of a 1-dimensional constructible set, part of Grothendieck's tame-topology 'analysis situs' drafts. The terminology (sommets redondants/lacunaires) is a nice detail, but the mathematics is folklore.
transcription_corrections: The script letter is Grothendieck's Φ (préfigure), as on neighbouring pages, not 𝔏.
The example préfigure is Φ = {a, S_ab, S_bc, c, S_cd, e}. The crossed marks are rewritten letters, not deletions, as confirmed by the next page's classification (a proper boundary, c redundant).
Φ̄ = {a, S_ab, b, S_bc, c, S_cd, d, e}; S_cd is not deleted.
Under 'card({X ∈ Φ_1 | a ◁ X})' the annotation reads Φ_1 = M_1 ∩ Φ (written '‖ M∩L' under Φ_1), not '𝔏_1 = M ∩ L'.
'Cet ordre est zéro si a n'est pas un sommet, mais il peut être zéro aussi pour un sommet de Φ'.
Page header '110' is Grothendieck's numbering; '119' is the archive folio.
